A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of racial disproportionality/disparity indicators can help child welfare agencies to: • Identify the extent of disproportionality and disparity in their service delivery; • Identify areas for further analysis and investigation; • Assess the effectiveness of interventions; • Identify areas of good practice; • Identify areas where further action is required; • Develop and monitor action plans to address disproportionality and disparity; • Identify areas requiring further research; • Monitor progress towards achieving equity in outcomes; • Inform policy development and resource allocation.

The main takeaway from our work is that

racial disproportionality and racial disparity indicators are not sufficient in themselves to measure the effectiveness of child welfare systems, but they do provide useful insights about how well the systems are performing in relation to the needs of black, indigenous and minority children.

child welfare systems need to be held accountable for the outcomes that they deliver to children, families, communities and society, and that racial disproportionality and racial disparity indicators can help to measure the effectiveness of child welfare services in this regard.
child welfare systems can be improved by using racial disproportionality and racial disparity indicators as part of a broader set of outcome measures.
